newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea won ends up, central bank said to step in.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea won ends up, central bank said to step in.

text.p: The won closed slightly higher on Monday after what dealers called was a heavy dollar selling by the central bank to slow the won's drop.
Bank of Korea officials denied it intervened as they routinely do.
The won was trading at the day's opening rate of 844.20 towards the close when the rumours of the intervention pushed up the won to end trading at 842.90, dealers said.
"The dollar was seen strongly supported at around the 842 won level by the still firm sentiment towards the dollar," said a dealer at SEOULBANK.
A foreign bank dealer also said many traders were willing to buy dollars at the 841-842 level and the dollar's bottom for the month would be over 840 won.
Dealers said the dollar's range on Tuesday would be slightly lower than Monday's because many traders were still worried over the central bank's intervention.
The Bank of Korea set won's base mid-rate at 844.00 for Tuesday, compared with 842.90 for Monday.
